title: Lesson — 10 November
description: From your lesson on 10 November: games and competitions, adjectives that describe stories and feelings, and types of text.

items.translation: знать что-то как свои пять пальцев
items.definition: to know every detail of something perfectly
items.example: She's played this game for years, so she [knows it inside and out].
items.exampleRu: Она играет в эту игру много лет, поэтому знает правила как свои пять пальцев.
collocations: know a city inside and out
know your job inside and out
items.pattern: know + noun + inside and out (BrE also: inside out)
items.trap: Not 'like my five fingers': that is a word-for-word Russian idiom English doesn't use.
wrong: know it like my five fingers

items.definition: a lot of new information that is hard to understand or accept all at once
items.example: The first day at the new job was [a lot to take in]: new people, new rules, new software.
items.exampleRu: Первый день на новой работе — это было много информации сразу: новые люди, новые правила, новая программа.
collocations: it's a lot to take in
items.pattern: it's / that's a lot to take in
items.trap: 'Take in' here means 'understand and remember', not 'take inside'.

items.definition: the stages of a game or competition; each one is played separately
items.example: The quiz has three [rounds], and the team with the most points wins.
items.exampleRu: В викторине три раунда, и побеждает команда, набравшая больше всего очков.
collocations: get through to the next round
items.pattern: the first / second / final round; win / lose a round
items.trap: A stage of a game is a 'round', not a 'raund' or 'tour' (a tour is a trip).

items.definition: a contest where you play up to three games and the first player to win two wins
items.example: You won the first game, but let's play [best of three] to make it fair.
items.exampleRu: Ты выиграл первую партию, но давай сыграем до двух побед из трёх, чтобы было честно.
items.pattern: let's play / let's make it best of three
items.trap: No 'from': say 'best of three', not 'two from three' or 'best from three'.

items.translation: начинать действовать, давать о себе знать
items.definition: to start to have an effect
items.example: I was nervous at the start, but then the adrenaline [kicked in] and I played really well.
items.exampleRu: Сначала я нервничал, но потом подействовал адреналин, и я сыграл очень хорошо.
items.pattern: something (medicine, coffee, nerves, a new rule) + kicks in
items.trap: No object: 'the coffee kicked in', not 'the coffee kicked me in'.

items.definition: exactly level with each other in a race or competition, so either could win
items.example: The two teams were [neck and neck] until the very last question.
items.exampleRu: Две команды шли ноздря в ноздрю до самого последнего вопроса.
collocations: neck and neck in the polls
items.pattern: be neck and neck (with sb)
items.trap: Not 'nose to nose' (that means face to face, often angrily).

items.definition: if a result comes down to something, that thing is what decides it in the end
items.example: In the end, the whole game [came down to] the last throw of the dice.
items.exampleRu: В итоге вся игра свелась к последнему броску кубика.
collocations: when it comes down to it
items.pattern: it (all) comes down to + noun / -ing
items.trap: Use 'to': 'it comes down to luck', not 'it comes down on luck' or 'it reduces to luck'.

items.definition: to react calmly to bad (or good) news, for example losing a game
items.example: My brother lost three games in a row, but he [took it well] and just laughed.
items.exampleRu: Мой брат проиграл три партии подряд, но воспринял это нормально и просто посмеялся.
items.pattern: take it / the news / defeat well / badly
items.trap: Not 'accept it good': the adverb is 'well', and the verb is 'take'.

items.definition: very sad, often because someone dies or something terrible happens
items.example: The film has a [tragic] ending, and half the cinema was crying.
items.exampleRu: У фильма трагичный конец, и половина зала плакала.
items.pattern: a tragic + ending / story / accident / loss
items.trap: Stress on the first syllable: TRA-gic. The noun is 'tragedy'.

items.definition: making you feel worried or upset
items.example: Some scenes in the documentary were quite [disturbing], so I don't recommend it for kids.
items.exampleRu: Некоторые сцены в документальном фильме довольно тревожные, так что детям я его не советую.
items.pattern: deeply / quite disturbing; find sth disturbing
items.trap: 'Disturbing' = upsetting. If something just interrupts you, use 'distracting' or 'annoying'.

items.definition: having a strong effect, or showing deep understanding
items.example: It's a short book, but it has a [profound] message about friendship.
items.exampleRu: Это короткая книга, но в ней глубокая мысль о дружбе.
items.pattern: a profound effect on / message / thought
items.trap: For water, use 'deep'. 'Profound' is for ideas, feelings and effects.

items.definition: fun and interesting to watch, read or listen to
items.example: The lecture was surprisingly [entertaining]: the professor told jokes the whole time.
items.exampleRu: Лекция оказалась на удивление занимательной: профессор всё время шутил.
items.pattern: very / highly entertaining; an entertaining read / evening
items.trap: The thing is 'entertaining'; the person is 'entertained': 'I was entertained', not 'I was entertaining'.

items.definition: making you believe that something is true or right
items.example: The actor was so [convincing] that I forgot it was a film.
items.exampleRu: Актёр был настолько убедительным, что я забыл, что это кино.
items.pattern: a convincing argument / reason / performance / win
items.trap: The argument is 'convincing'; you are 'convinced': 'I'm convinced', not 'I'm convincing'.

items.definition: not making you believe that something is true or real
items.example: The ending felt [unconvincing]: nobody would act like that in real life.
items.exampleRu: Концовка показалась неубедительной: в реальной жизни так никто бы не поступил.
items.pattern: an unconvincing excuse / explanation / ending
items.trap: One word with 'un-': not 'not convincing enough' every time, and not 'inconvincing'.

items.definition: making you annoyed because you can't do what you want
items.example: It's so [frustrating] when the game freezes just before you win.
items.exampleRu: Так досадно, когда игра зависает прямо перед твоей победой.
items.pattern: it's frustrating when / that …; find sth frustrating
items.trap: The situation is 'frustrating'; you feel 'frustrated'. Not the Russian 'фрустрация' idea of deep depression: it's everyday annoyance.

items.definition: making you feel happy and satisfied because it's useful or important
items.example: Teaching kids isn't well paid, but it's a really [fulfilling] job.
items.exampleRu: Учить детей — не очень денежно, но это работа, которая приносит настоящее удовлетворение.
items.pattern: a fulfilling job / career / life / experience
items.trap: Spelling: fulfil (BrE) → fulfilling, double l. It means 'satisfying', not 'full' or 'busy'.

items.definition: wanting very much to do or have something
items.example: The new players were [eager] to show what they could do.
items.exampleRu: Новые игроки горели желанием показать, на что они способны.
items.pattern: be eager to + verb; be eager for + noun
items.trap: Use 'to + verb': 'eager to win', not 'eager for winning' or 'eager of winning'.

items.definition: so bad, weak or useless that it makes you annoyed or a little sad
items.example: That was a [pathetic] excuse: 'my dog ate my homework'?
items.exampleRu: Это была жалкая отговорка: «собака съела мою домашку»?
items.pattern: a pathetic excuse / attempt / performance
items.trap: False friend: not 'патетический' (= emotional, grand). For grand, emotional speech say 'emotional' or 'dramatic'.

items.definition: giving you hope or confidence
items.example: The first results are [encouraging], so we'll keep going.
items.exampleRu: Первые результаты обнадёживают, поэтому мы продолжим.
items.pattern: encouraging news / results / sign / words
items.trap: The news is 'encouraging'; you feel 'encouraged'.

items.definition: so big or strong that it's hard to deal with
items.example: Starting a new job, moving house and studying at the same time was [overwhelming].
items.exampleRu: Начать новую работу, переехать и учиться одновременно — это было непосильно.
items.pattern: find sth overwhelming; an overwhelming majority / feeling
items.trap: Silent 'h' after w: /ˌəʊvəˈwelmɪŋ/. The thing is 'overwhelming'; you feel 'overwhelmed'.

items.translation: фанфикшн (истории, написанные поклонниками по мотивам известных произведений)
items.definition: stories written by fans using characters or worlds from a famous book, film or series
items.example: She writes [fanfiction] about Harry Potter and posts it online.
items.exampleRu: Она пишет фанфики по «Гарри Поттеру» и выкладывает их в интернет.
items.pattern: write / read fanfiction (uncountable); a fanfic (countable, informal)
items.trap: Uncountable: 'I write fanfiction', not 'I write a fanfiction'. For one story say 'a fanfic'.

items.definition: books and stories about imaginary people and events
items.example: I mostly read [fiction], but this year I'm trying some history books too.
items.exampleRu: Я в основном читаю художественную литературу, но в этом году пробую и книги по истории.
items.pattern: read fiction; a work of fiction; fiction vs non-fiction
items.trap: Not 'artistic literature' (word-for-word from Russian). Uncountable: not 'a fiction'.

items.definition: a short text, photo or video that someone shares on Instagram, Facebook, etc.
items.example: His [social media post] about the match got thousands of likes.
items.exampleRu: Его пост в соцсетях о матче набрал тысячи лайков.
collocations: write / share a social media post
items.pattern: write / share / delete a social media post; a post on + platform
items.trap: 'Post' is both the noun and the verb: 'I posted it', not 'I made a post it'. Say 'on social media', not 'in social media'.

items.definition: an article or comment giving an opinion about a book, film, product, etc.
items.example: The film got great [reviews], so we bought tickets for Friday.
items.exampleRu: У фильма отличные рецензии, поэтому мы купили билеты на пятницу.
items.pattern: a review of + film / book / product; get good reviews
items.trap: Not 'recension' (that's a rare academic word). Say 'a review of the film', not 'a review about the film' in most cases.

items.definition: a formal document that explains what a study found
items.example: Our team spent two months on the [research report] about customer habits.
items.exampleRu: Наша команда два месяца работала над исследовательским отчётом о привычках клиентов.
items.pattern: write / publish a research report on / into sth
items.trap: 'Research' is uncountable: 'a lot of research', not 'researches'.

items.definition: a text that explains step by step how to do something
items.example: I followed a [how-to guide] on YouTube and fixed the washing machine myself.
items.exampleRu: Я посмотрел пошаговую инструкцию на YouTube и сам починил стиральную машину.
items.pattern: write / follow a how-to guide (on sth)
items.trap: Not 'instruction' (that's usually plural and from the maker: 'instructions'). A text you read online is 'a how-to guide'.

items.definition: a funny piece of writing in a magazine, newspaper or online
items.example: He wrote a [humorous article] about the worst holiday he's ever had.
items.exampleRu: Он написал юмористическую статью о самом неудачном отпуске в своей жизни.
items.pattern: a humorous article / story / tone / style
items.trap: Spelling: 'humour' (BrE) but 'humorous' (no u before r). Not 'humoristic'.
